findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — Sync requests identify a credential only by userId and appSlug, so users with multiple accounts for one app can receive and persist a token for the wrong provider account.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — The webhook blindly overwrites credentials without an issued-at or version guard, so a delayed retry or replay can roll a user back to an older revoked token.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:203 — Shared-refresh failures are swallowed while the module-global HubSpot client retains its prior token, allowing the request to continue against another user's account.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:61 — Lark deletes the credential before consulting the sync endpoint when the local refresh token is missing or expired, defeating remote refresh and irreversibly disconnecting the app.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — In sharing mode the minimum parser strips instance_url before this replacement write, so the next Salesforce client cannot target the account's instance.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — Shared refresh replaces the real refresh token with the fabricated "refresh_token" placeholder, making later local fallback unable to recover during a sync outage or configuration rollback.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:77 — Updating fresh keys does not clear an existing invalid flag, so a successfully resynchronized credential can remain silently disabled.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync path returns a Fetch Response but this caller reads Axios-style res.data, so Google refreshes cannot consume the endpoint response.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safe-parse wrapper, so Google persists {success,data} instead of the credential shape after every local refresh.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The sync path returns a Fetch Response but this caller treats it as HubspotToken, producing undefined token fields and a broken refreshed credential.
packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — The advertised flat access-token-and-expiry sync response cannot satisfy this caller's required nested Lark data and refresh-token fields.
packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — The advertised minimal sync response is rejected because this caller still requires provider-specific scope, token type, and refresh-token fields.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys are literal property names rather than catch-all rules, so expiry and other endpoint fields are silently stripped.
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens and always calls Salesforce directly, so it never honors the configured credential-sync endpoint.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Invalid bodies, ciphertext, or decrypted JSON throw uncaught parser errors, exposing a 500 response instead of a stable client-error contract.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Shared refresh returns a Fetch `Response`, so reading `res.data` throws and leaves Google using the expired credential.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the SafeParse wrapper, so every successful Google refresh stores `{success,data}` instead of the credential fields.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Shared refresh returns a Fetch `Response` but this code treats it as a `HubspotToken`, producing undefined token fields and invalid persisted credentials.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential-sharing mode still sends the local refresh token directly to Salesforce instead of using the configured sync endpoint.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — The shared endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry, but Webex still requires provider scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh expiry and therefore rejects a conforming response.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — A minimal shared-endpoint token response is parsed as Lark's nested provider response, so conforming sync responses cannot refresh Lark credentials.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:83 — Concurrent first deliveries can both miss `findFirst` and create duplicate credentials for the same user and app.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — Returning `any` while switching between native responses and provider-specific token objects hides incompatible contracts that break the Google and HubSpot sync paths

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Recomputing the sync branch without the credential user context makes team credentials use provider refresh with the unrelated sync-response schema

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:65 — The non-atomic find-then-create path lets concurrent webhook retries create duplicate credentials that later updates may leave stale.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every Salesforce adapter initialization now depends on an unconditional token-endpoint call, so a transient OAuth outage blocks operations even while the stored access token is valid.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:35 — Any accepted team member can create a team-wide OAuth credential because the team branch never enforces admin access

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4 — The new shared-token branch has no tests using a real Fetch Response or exercising enabled, disabled, and team-owned fallback paths.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:24 — Credential ownership branching has no tests for unauthenticated, user-owned, team-member, and team-admin cases.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — Sync requests identify a credential only by userId and appSlug, so users with multiple accounts for one app can receive and persist a token for the wrong provider account.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it sends only calcomUserId and appSlug to the sync endpoint. The credential table can have multiple credentials per user per app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts). The sync endpoint at app-credential.ts uses findFirst with userId and appId, which would return an arbitrary credential if multiple exist. This means tokens could be persisted to the wrong credential record when a user has multiple accounts for the same app.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — The webhook blindly overwrites credentials without an issued-at or version guard, so a delayed retry or replay can roll a user back to an older revoked token.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a legitimate architectural concern in the new webhook endpoint. Looking at lines 68-91 in app-credential.ts, the code does a simple findFirst/update or create pattern without any timestamp, version, or idempotency check. If webhooks arrive out of order or are replayed, newer credentials could be overwritten by older ones. This is a valid design concern for the new credential sync feature, though it's more of a missing safeguard than a definite bug - it depends on the external system's behavior and whether replay/ordering issues actually occur in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:203 — Shared-refresh failures are swallowed while the module-global HubSpot client retains its prior token, allowing the request to continue against another user's account.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper is added around the token refresh call, but the finding claims failures are 'swallowed' and the module-global client retains prior tokens. However, the diff shows the existing error handling pattern remains unchanged - the try/catch block and error handling logic are preserved. The refreshOAuthTokens function in the diff (lines 3-22 of refreshOAuthTokens.ts) simply returns the response from either the sync endpoint or the original refresh function - it doesn't swallow errors. The finding mischaracterizes what the code does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The sync path returns a Fetch Response but this caller treats it as HubspotToken, producing undefined token fields and a broken refreshed credential.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken call with refreshOAuthTokens. The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of refreshFunction(). When credential sync is enabled, it returns a raw fetch Response, but the code expects HubspotToken type with properties like accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn. The code then uses hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken, hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn etc. on line 191+, which would be undefined on a Response object. This is a real type mismatch bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — The advertised flat access-token-and-expiry sync response cannot satisfy this caller's required nested Lark data and refresh-token fields.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (lines 3-21 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either the response from the external CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT or the result of refreshFunction(). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it returns a fetch Response object from the sync endpoint. The original code expected to call handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log) on the response, which expects Lark's specific nested response structure with data.access_token, data.refresh_token, etc. The sync endpoint is documented to return only 'access_token and expiry date' (per comment in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 7), which won't have Lark's nested structure or refresh_token. This mismatch would cause handleLarkError to fail or return incorrect data when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — The advertised minimal sync response is rejected because this caller still requires provider-specific scope, token type, and refresh-token fields.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, the refreshAccessToken function now uses refreshOAuthTokens wrapper (lines 62-79). The response is then passed to handleWebexResponse (line 81). The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in the diff at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) uses minimumTokenResponseSchema when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, which only requires access_token and a number field. However, handleWebexResponse in webex likely expects the full Webex token structure. Looking at the code flow, the response from refreshOAuthTokens goes directly to handleWebexResponse without going through parseRefreshTokenResponse - unlike other integrations like zoom or office365 that explicitly call parseRefreshTokenResponse. So the webex integration doesn't use parseRefreshTokenResponse at all, meaning this finding appears to be a hallucination about how the code works.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys are literal property names rather than catch-all rules, so expiry and other endpoint fields are silently stripped.
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens and always calls Salesforce directly, so it never honors the configured credential-sync endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, lines 72-89 show a direct fetch call to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' without using the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper that other integrations use. Comparing to other calendar services in the diff (Google, Office365, Lark, Zoho, etc.), they all wrap their refresh token calls with refreshOAuthTokens(). Salesforce directly calls fetch() and then uses parseRefreshTokenResponse, but skips the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper that would honor CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. This is inconsistent with the pattern established for other integrations and means Salesforce won't use the credential sync endpoint when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code adds new functionality that uses `prisma.credential.update()` at line 87-90 (in the new code around line 96 in the full file). However, examining the imports shown in the diff, only `getAppKeysFromSlug` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` are imported - there is no import statement for `prisma`. The existing code in the file (before the diff) may or may not have had prisma imported, but the diff shows imports being added without adding a prisma import, and the new code clearly uses `prisma.credential.update()`. This would cause a runtime error when the code tries to use an undefined `prisma` variable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Shared refresh returns a Fetch `Response`, so reading `res.data` throws and leaves Google using the expired credential.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the code now calls `refreshOAuthTokens()` which wraps the refresh function. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response` object directly (line 11-14 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts). However, the code at line 94 tries to access `res?.data` which is the Google API response format, not the fetch Response format. A fetch Response doesn't have a `.data` property - you need to call `.json()` on it. This would cause `token` to be undefined, breaking the credential refresh when credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the SafeParse wrapper, so every successful Google refresh stores `{success,data}` instead of the credential fields.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts line 100, the code changes from `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` - a SafeParseResult object with `{success, data}` structure. This object is then stored directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The old code used `.parse()` which returns the parsed data directly, but the new code returns the SafeParse wrapper. This would store `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of just the credential fields, corrupting the stored credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Shared refresh returns a Fetch `Response` but this code treats it as a `HubspotToken`, producing undefined token fields and invalid persisted credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. The `refreshOAuthTokens` function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of `refreshFunction()`. In the Hubspot case, `refreshFunction` returns `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` which returns a HubspotToken. However, when credential sharing is enabled, the function returns a raw fetch Response, not a HubspotToken. The code then treats `hubspotRefreshToken` as a HubspotToken object (accessing properties like `accessToken`, `expiresIn`), which would be undefined on a Response object. This is a type mismatch bug that would cause incorrect credential storage when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Both computed Zod keys collapse to the literal `"[object Object]"`, so advertised numeric expiry fields are stripped from shared refresh responses.
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the computed property keys in the Zod schema using [z.string().toString()] syntax. The golden comment explains this is invalid Zod syntax that will throw a runtime error, while the candidate comment explains the specific consequence - that these computed keys collapse to '[object Object]' literal strings. Both are pointing to the same bug with the Zod schema definition, just describing different aspects of the problem (invalid syntax vs. the specific behavior of toString() on Zod objects).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential-sharing mode still sends the local refresh token directly to Salesforce instead of using the configured sync endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts (lines 72-91), the code directly calls fetch() to refresh tokens without wrapping it in refreshOAuthTokens(). Other calendar services like Google, Office365, Zoom, etc. all wrap their refresh token calls with refreshOAuthTokens() to support credential sharing mode. Salesforce's implementation bypasses this pattern entirely - it directly posts to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' with the local refresh_token. This means when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured, Salesforce will still use local refresh tokens instead of the sync endpoint, which is inconsistent with the credential sharing feature being implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — The shared endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry, but Webex still requires provider scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh expiry and therefore rejects a conforming response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, the code wraps the refresh token fetch in refreshOAuthTokens(). According to refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it calls the external endpoint instead of the refreshFunction. The parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts shows that when credential sharing is enabled, it uses minimumTokenResponseSchema which only validates access_token and a number (expiry). However, the Webex VideoApiAdapter at line 88+ processes responseBody expecting the full Webex token response structure (access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_token_expires_in, token_type). The finding correctly identifies that when using the shared endpoint, the response won't contain all the fields Webex code expects, potentially causing issues. However, looking more carefully at the code flow - handleWebexResponse is called on the response, and the Webex adapter doesn't use parseRefreshTokenResponse directly. The refreshOAuthTokens just returns the fetch response, which then goes through handleWebexResponse. So the actual token parsing happens after. The issue is that the shared endpoint returns a minimal response that may not have refresh_token, but the Webex code expects it. This is a valid concern about compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — A minimal shared-endpoint token response is parsed as Lark's nested provider response, so conforming sync responses cannot refresh Lark credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens() but then passes the response directly to handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either the response from the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT or the result of refreshFunction(). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the sync endpoint returns a minimal token response (access_token + expiry), but handleLarkError expects Lark's nested response structure (RefreshTokenResp). This mismatch means the Lark-specific parsing will fail when credential sharing is enabled, as the sync endpoint's response format won't match Lark's expected nested structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:83 — Concurrent first deliveries can both miss `findFirst` and create duplicate credentials for the same user and app.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a findFirst followed by conditional create pattern in app-credential.ts (lines 57-88). If two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId and appSlug, both could execute findFirst before either creates a credential, resulting in both finding null and both creating duplicate credentials. This is a classic race condition - the code lacks any transaction or unique constraint enforcement visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — Returning `any` while switching between native responses and provider-specific token objects hides incompatible contracts that break the Google and HubSpot sync paths

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens returns `any` type (line 3: `async (refreshFunction: () => any, appSlug: string, userId: number | null)`). Looking at the diff, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it returns a fetch Response object, but when false, it returns whatever refreshFunction() returns. For Google Calendar (line 83-91), refreshFunction returns `fetchTokens.res` which is a Google API response, while for HubSpot (line 176-191), it returns the hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken result directly. These have different structures. The `any` return type masks this contract mismatch. However, this is more of a type safety/architecture concern than a definite bug since the code paths may work at runtime - it's an important design issue but not a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed Zod object keys stringify to a literal property instead of accepting arbitrary numeric fields, so the shared schema strips expiry and provider metadata

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys. In JavaScript/TypeScript, `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a string like '[object Object]' or similar literal string, not a dynamic key pattern. This means the schema won't actually accept arbitrary numeric fields for expiry dates or other provider metadata - it will only match literal property names that equal the stringified Zod type. This is a real bug that would cause the minimumTokenResponseSchema to fail validation for legitimate token responses that contain expiry fields like 'expires_in' or 'expiry_date'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Recomputing the sync branch without the credential user context makes team credentials use provider refresh with the unrelated sync-response schema

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that parseRefreshTokenResponse at line 15 has an issue with team credentials and sync-response schema. Looking at the diff, parseRefreshTokenResponse takes a response and schema parameter, and uses APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED to decide whether to use minimumTokenResponseSchema or the provided schema. The function doesn't have any 'credential user context' parameter - it simply validates token responses. The finding's claim about 'team credentials use provider refresh with unrelated sync-response schema' is not verifiable from the diff. The function logic is straightforward: if credential sharing is enabled, use a minimal schema; otherwise use the provided schema. There's no evidence of the described bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — Fabricating a `refresh_token` couples every provider to an invalid sentinel and overwrites Office 365's usable stored refresh token

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 24-26, when refresh_token is missing from the response, the code sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. This fabricated value then gets stored in the database. In Office365CalendarService.ts line 256, the code does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` which would overwrite the existing valid refresh_token with this fake 'refresh_token' string if the response doesn't include a new refresh_token. This would break subsequent token refreshes since the stored refresh_token would be invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — The parser returns a SafeParse envelope, so this call stores `{success,data}` instead of the Google credential payload

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 97 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 98-100 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` - this returns a SafeParseResult object with `{success, data, error}` structure, not the actual parsed data. The code should be using `refreshTokenResponse.data` instead of the whole SafeParseResult object when storing to the database.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — Decrypted JSON is persisted without an app-specific credential schema, leaking an unvalidated external shape into every integration's stored credential boundary

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every Salesforce adapter construction now makes an unconditional token request and credential write even when the stored access token is still valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync branch returns a raw Fetch Response to callers expecting incompatible SDK or provider-specific shapes, so Google, HubSpot, Lark, and Webex refreshes fail when credential sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The sync-endpoint fetch has no abort timeout, so a hung server pins every calendar or video request awaiting token refresh until the hosting platform kills it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens.ts at lines 6-14 making a fetch call to process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without any timeout/AbortController. This is a valid concern - if the external endpoint hangs, the request will block indefinitely. However, this is not strictly a 'bug' (the code will work correctly when the endpoint responds), but rather a missing defensive programming practice for a new feature. It's a legitimate architectural concern about the new credential sync functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:32 — Malformed bodies, ciphertext, or decrypted JSON throw uncaught exceptions and return 500, causing webhook senders to retry permanent input failures.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, line 32 shows `const reqBody = appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);` which throws on invalid input. Lines 55-57 show `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` - both symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse can throw exceptions on malformed ciphertext or invalid JSON. There's no try-catch wrapper around these operations, so they would result in uncaught exceptions returning 500 errors. This is a real bug - permanent input failures (malformed data) would cause 500s that webhook senders typically retry, when they should return 4xx to indicate the request itself is invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:65 — The non-atomic find-then-create path lets concurrent webhook retries create duplicate credentials that later updates may leave stale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a find-then-create pattern in app-credential.ts lines 57-85: first findFirst is called to check if credential exists, then either update or create is performed. This is not atomic - if two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId/appId, both could pass the findFirst check (returning null), and both would then attempt to create new credentials, resulting in duplicate entries. This is a real race condition bug in the new webhook endpoint code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every Salesforce adapter initialization now depends on an unconditional token-endpoint call, so a transient OAuth outage blocks operations even while the stored access token is valid.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the diff shows that lines 72-88 add an unconditional fetch call to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' during the initialization of the Salesforce connection (in the constructor or connection setup). This happens before the jsforce.Connection is created. Unlike other integrations that use refreshOAuthTokens which conditionally refreshes based on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the Salesforce implementation makes this token refresh call unconditionally every time. This means if the OAuth endpoint is temporarily unavailable, the entire Salesforce adapter initialization will fail, even if the existing stored access_token is still valid and could be used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Credential-sync requests send only guessable user and app identifiers without authenticating Cal.com to the token-issuing endpoint

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the code sends a POST request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There's no authentication header or secret being sent to verify that Cal.com is the legitimate caller. This contrasts with the webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) which validates CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header. The credential sync endpoint request lacks any authentication mechanism, making it vulnerable to unauthorized token requests if an attacker knows the endpoint URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET makes a headerless request pass the webhook authentication check when sharing is otherwise enabled

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the authentication check compares the header value against process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then undefined === undefined evaluates to true, bypassing authentication. The APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED check at line 17-19 requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET to be set (from packages/lib/constants.ts), but this is a truthy check - an empty string would fail that check. However, if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is somehow unset at runtime but APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED was evaluated as truthy during build/initialization, this could be a security issue. The finding identifies a real potential authentication bypass vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4 — The new shared-token branch has no tests using a real Fetch Response or exercising enabled, disabled, and team-owned fallback paths.
